 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice V.Gopala Krishna Rao

entities.text: United India Insurance Company ... vs Challa Akkamma
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The appellant is 2nd respondent/Insurance company and the respondents are claim petitioners and respondent Nos.1 and 3 in M.V.O.P.No.214 of 2016 on the file of the Chairman, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-II Additional District Judge (Fast Track Court), Srikakulam.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-II Additional District Judge (Fast Track Court), Srikakulam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The appellant filed the appeal questioning the legal validity of the order of the Tribunal.
2. For the sake of convenience, both the parties in the appeal will be referred to as they are arrayed in the claim petition.

3. The claim petitioners filed the petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 read with Rule 455 of the A.P.M.V. Rules, 1989 against the respondents claiming compensation of Rs.3,00,000/- for the death of Ch.Bharathi, who is daughter-in-law of the 1st petitioner and mother of petitioner Nos.2 to 4, in a motor vehicle accident that took place on 02.02.2005.
VGKR,J 4.

The brief averments in the petition filed by the petitioners are as follows:
On 02.02.2005 the deceased along with her husband boarded a lorry bearing registration No.16X 6309 of the 1st respondent to reach Sasanam village and when the said lorry reached Sasanam village, the driver of the said lorry drove the same in a rash and negligent manner at high speed, and at that time, the driver of one bus bearing registration No.OR 22 3114 owned by the 3rd respondent also drove the bus in a rash and negligent manner at high speed and both the vehicles dashed against each other resulting in the instantaneous death of the deceased and her husband.

The 1st respondent is owner and the 2nd respondent is insurer of the lorry and the 3rd respondent is owner of the bus, hence, all the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
5. Respondent Nos.1 and 3 were set ex parte.
The 2nd respondent filed a written statement by denying the manner of accident, age, avocation and income of the deceased.

It is pleaded that the deceased was travelling in the offending lorry as a gratuitous VGKR,J passenger at the time of accident and the claim of the petitioners is very exorbitant.
6. Based on the above pleadings of both the parties, the following issues were settled for trial by the Tribunal:

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Whether the deceased Challa Bharathi wife of late malleus died on account of the injuries suffered by her in the motor vehicle accident that took place on 2.2.2005 at 2.15 p.m. at Sasanam village on NH5 road in Nandigam Police Station limits of Srikakulam District?

If so, the said accident had only occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the lorry AP 16X 6309 by its driver or due to the rash and negligent driving of the OSRTC bus No.OR 22 3114 by its driver?
2) Whether the petitioners are entitled to claim any compensation for the death of deceased Challa Bharathi wife of late Mallesu?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
3) To what relief?
7.
During the course of enquiry in the claim petition, on behalf of the petitioners, P.Ws.1 and 2 were examined and Exs.A.1 to A.5 were marked.

On behalf of the 2nd respondent/Insurance company,
R.W.1 was examined and Ex.B.1 was marked.
VGKR,J 8.

At the culmination of the enquiry, based on the material available on record, the Tribunal came to the conclusion that the accident in question took place due to contributory negligence on the part of the drivers of both the lorry and the bus, and accordingly, allowed the petition in part and granted an amount of Rs.2,65,000/- towards compensation to petitioner Nos.2 to 4 with proportionate costs and interest at 7.5% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of payment and directed the 2nd respondent/Insurance company to pay 50% of the compensation to the petitioners in first and later recover the same from the 1st respondent/owner by filing an execution petition and also directed the 3rd respondent to pay the remaining 50% of the compensation and dismissed the claim of the 1st petitioner.
Questioning the legal validity of the order of the Tribunal, the 2 nd respondent/Insurance company preferred the instant appeal.
9. Heard learned counsels for both the parties and perused the record.
VGKR,J 10.

Learned counsel for the appellant/Insurance company contended that the deceased was travelling in the offending lorry at the time of accident as an unauthorized passenger and her risk was not covered under Ex.B.1 policy, as such, the Insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation.

11. Now, the point for determination is:
Whether the order of the Tribunal needs any interference of this Court, if so, to what extent?

sentences.text: 12. POINT:

In order to prove the rash and negligent driving of the drivers of the offending vehicles,
the petitioners relied on the evidence of P.Ws.1 and 2 as well as Exs.A.1 and A.2.
P.W.1 is none other than the mother-in-law of the deceased and she is not an eye witness to the accident.
She reiterated the contents of the petition in her chief examination affidavit.
P.W.2 is an eye witness to the accident.

According to P.W.2, on 02.02.2005 at about 2.15 p.m. while he was at Sasanam village junction for bus to Tekkali, the driver of a lorry, which was coming from Palasa, drove it in a rash and negligent manner and at the same time, one bus coming from Srikakulam side VGKR,J also came in a rash and negligent manner and both the vehicles dashed against each other resulting in severe injuries to the deceased and her husband and later they succumbed to injuries while undergoing treatment in the hospital.
P.W.2 also deposed that the accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of the drivers of both the offending vehicles.
As seen from Exs.A.1-first information report and Ex.A.2-charge sheet, nowhere it is mentioned in Exs.A.1 and A.2 that the accident was a head on collision in between the lorry and the bus.

In order to rebut the evidence of P.Ws. 1 and 2 or to establish their case that there was no fault on the part of the driver of the offending lorry and that the accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending bus alone, the 2 nd respondent/Insurance company did not place any iota of evidence before the Tribunal.
Further, the 3rd respondent/owner of the offending bus was set ex parte.
In view of the above reasons, this Court is of the opinion that the accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the drivers of both the offending vehicles.
On appreciation of the entire material on record, the Tribunal also VGKR,J came to the same conclusion.
Therefore, there is no need to interfere with the said finding given by the Tribunal.

13. Coming to the compensation, since there is no evidence on record to show that the deceased was earning Rs.2,000/- as deposed by P.W.1, by relying on the provisions of the Minimum Wages Act,
the Tribunal fixed the monthly income of the deceased as Rs.1,800/- i.e., Rs.21,600/- per annum.

As per Ex.A.2-charge sheet and Ex.A.5-post mortem certificate, the age of the deceased was 35 years at the time of accident and by taking into consideration the II Schedule to Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act, the Tribunal took the multiplier applicable to the age group of the deceased as '16'.
The dependents on the deceased are three in number.

After deducting 1/3rd from out of the annual income towards personal expenses of the deceased and by applying the multiplier '16', the Tribunal rightly arrived the loss of dependency to the family members of the deceased at Rs.2,30,400/-
(Rs.14,400/- (Rs.21,600/- - Rs.7,200/-) x multiplier "16").

In addition to that, the Tribunal granted Rs.10,000/- each towards loss of love and affection to petitioner Nos.2 to 4, Rs.2,000/-
VGKR,J towards funeral expenses of the deceased, and Rs.2,500/- towards loss of estate.
By giving cogent reasons, the Tribunal came to the conclusion that petitioner Nos.2 to 4 are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.2,65,000/-.

The Tribunal rightly held in its order that the 1st petitioner is mother-in-law of the deceased and she is neither class-I legal her nor dependent on the deceased, as such, she is not entitled for any compensation.
There is no legal flaw or infirmity in the said findings given by the Tribunal.

14. It is not in dispute that the offending lorry of the 1st respondent was insured with the 2nd respondent/Insurance company under Ex.B.1 policy and the policy was also in force as on the date of accident.

15. As stated supra, the accident in question occurred because of contributory negligence on the part of the drivers of both the lorry and the bus.

On considering the material available on record, the Tribunal rightly held in its order that respondent Nos.1 and 2 being owner and insurer of the offending lorry and the 3rd respondent/owner of the bus VGKR,J are liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners equally i.e., @ 50% each.
Therefore, there is no need to interfere with the said finding given by the Tribunal.

16. It is the contention of the learned counsel for the appellant/2 nd respondent-Insurance company that the Insurance company is not liable to pay even 50% of the compensation, since the deceased travelled in the offending lorry as an unauthorized passenger and her risk was not covered under Ex.B.1 policy.
17. Admittedly, the deceased and her husband travelled in the offending lorry as unauthorized passengers at the relevant point of time.
A perusal of Ex.B.1 policy, the owner of the lorry paid an additional premium of Rs.75/- to cover the risk of one non-fair paying passenger.

In view of the same and on considering the fact that the petitioners are third parties, the Tribunal rightly directed the 2nd respondent/Insurance company to pay 50% of the compensation to the petitioners in the first instance and later recover the same from the 1st respondent/owner of the offending lorry by filing an execution VGKR,J petition without filing any independent suit.
Therefore, there is no need to interfere with the said finding given by the Tribunal.

18. In similar circumstances, in Anu Bhanvara Vs. Iffco Tokio General insurance Company Limited1,
a three-Judge Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that the principle of 'pay and recover'
should be directed to be invoked in the present case.

entities.text: Anu Bhanvara Vs. Iffco Tokio General insurance Company Limited1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 19. For the foregoing discussion, I do not find any illegality or irregularity in the impugned order of the Tribunal and it is perfectly sustainable under law and the appeal is devoid of merits, therefore, it is liable to be dismissed.

20. Accordingly, the appeal is dismissed, while confirming the decree and order dated 23.04.2009 passed by the Chairman, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-II Additional District Judge (Fast Track Court), Srikakulam, in M.V.O.P.No.214 of 2006.
